messages:
Maria (Docs): Heads-up — I found 4 broken anchors and a couple of outdated SDK snippets in the Dedicated provisioning guide. Putting together a small PR to fix links + update the autoscale example. PTAL? PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4567
Jon (ENG): thanks, can you call out which autoscale examples are stale?
Maria (Docs): the main one under /dedicated/provisioning/autoscale.md — the YAML uses old fields: `scalePolicy` -> `scale_policies`, and the tenant label example is using `tenant_id` instead of `tenant_label`. Also the sample k8s annotation block is missing the isolation decorator note.
Lee (Infra): yep we changed the annotation key last quarter. I can paste the corrected snippet.
Lee (Infra): ```yaml
# suggested autoscale snippet
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: dedicated-autoscale
  annotations:
    redwood.com/isolation: "reserved-pool"
data:
  scale_policies: |
    - name: default
      min: 1
      max: 10
```
Sasha (ML): also the quantization recommendation paragraph references an old model family (rwkv). We should replace with a short blurb about per-workload quant vs batch sizing. I can draft a 2-sentence replacement.
Alex (Docs): Maria — can you add a changelog note for the handbook index? We want traceability for prod-facing wording changes (SLA phrasing).
Maria (Docs): good call. I also want to tweak SLA wording. Current line: "Redwood Dedicated offers a 99.95% uptime SLA for reserved pools." Suggest: "Redwood Dedicated: 99.95% availability for in-region reserved capacity; cross-region failover not covered by this SLA." Any objections?
Jon (ENG): sounds clearer to me. Maybe add a short example scenario under the SLA section (e.g., regional outage -> fallback behavior).
Lee (Infra): can we also include a tiny decision table for eviction/isolation precedence? A 2-row table: reserved vs shared, which gets preempted.
Maria (Docs): yes — I'll add a mini table and reference to the isolation runbook. Need the canonical link for the runbook. @Lee can you paste it?
Lee (Infra): linking: https://internal.redwood.com/runbooks/isolation-handbook (internal)
Sasha (ML): On the SDK snippet: the TypeScript example uses old client API `createDedicatedPool`. New API is `reserveCapacity` and returns a `poolId`. Update needed.
Alex (Docs): For the docs test harness, can we add a small doc-only unit that renders the YAML snippet and checks anchors? Might prevent regressions on future link shuffles.
Jon (ENG): +1. We have a tiny CI job that validates markdown anchors. I'll add the config to .github/workflows/docs-link-check.yml in the PR branch.
Maria (Docs): sweet — plan: I will open a new commit on PR #4567 with: 1) fixed anchors, 2) updated autoscale YAML (Lee's snippet), 3) SLA rewording + example scenario, 4) updated TS SDK snippet (Sasha's note), 5) changelog entry, 6) add docs link-check workflow. Will ping when ready for review.
Alex (Docs): would be great to include a one-line migration note at the top: "If you relied on scalePolicy or createDedicatedPool, see migration notes below."
Maria (Docs): added to my todo. ETA EOD.
deploy-bot: CI: docs-link-check passed on branch maria/provisioning-link-fix :white_check_mark:
Jon (ENG): quick ask — can we keep the autoscale example under 40 lines? It's easier for readers.
Lee (Infra): yes I'll trim comments and move longer explanation into a collapsible section.
Sasha (ML): if you want I can drop a short eval note about latency impact when using prefix cache vs full KV cache. One sentence under caching recommendations.
Maria (Docs): perfect. Thanks all — I'll @mention reviewers when PR is up. :thumbsup:
